title: SDLC-to-IR: Traceable Authorization Change Evidence Playbook
author: Asha Menon
content:
Summary

This playbook defines a reproducible, end-to-end approach for capturing, packaging, and delivering authorization-related evidence across the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) into Incident Response (IR) workflows. It ensures that changes to entitlements, policy rules, attribute mappings, and related CI/CD artifacts can be reconstructed and delivered to auditors and IR teams within defined SLOs while preserving residency and retention constraints.

Purpose and scope

- Purpose: Reduce triage time for incidents related to authorization, privilege escalation, and entitlement drift by making evidence traceable from developer commit -> CI build -> deployment -> runtime authorization event.
- Scope: Applies to all services that control access to customer or internal data (Redwood API, Private Control Plane, Dedicated GPU orchestration service, internal admin consoles). Does NOT replace broader legal evidence preservation directives; follow legal hold guidance for customer-impacting incidents.

Ownership and escalation

- Policy owner: Security (Access Controls) squad (primary).
- Operational owner: Eng-platform (CI/CD) for artifact provenance; Eng-sre for runtime log access; Security for audit/evidence packaging and handoff.
- Escalation path: Security on-call -> Eng-sre on-call -> Legal (if preservation order issued).

High-level requirements

1) Every authorization configuration change must be linked to a source artifact (PR/commit ID).
2) CI/CD must produce immutable build metadata (artifact ID, build timestamp, signed checksum) and publish it to the provenance store.
3) Runtime authorization decisions must emit correlated audit events containing the minimal provenance keys (service, request_id, principal_hash, artifact_id).
4) Evidence bundles for incidents must be assembled within SLOs and contain a minimal manifest (see "Bundle manifest" section).

Traceability model (keys and correlations)

- principal_id: internal ID for the actor (user/service) performing a change.
- change_request_id: PR or change ticket reference (e.g., GH-12345, JIRA-SEC-2024).
- artifact_id: immutable CI artifact identifier (e.g., artifact://build-20251112-abcdef).
- deployment_id: deployment rollout identifier (e.g., rollout:redwood-api-prod-20251112-3).
- request_id: runtime request ID that can be correlated back to deployment and artifact.

Minimum event schema (example)

All events that are relevant to authorization should include these top-level fields in the audit stream (JSON line event):

{
  "timestamp": "2026-02-28T14:23:00Z",
  "event_type": "authz_change",
  "service": "admin-portal",
  "principal_id": "acct-1024",
  "change_request_id": "GH-1428",
  "artifact_id": "artifact://build-20251112-abcdef",
  "diff": "(json patch) ...",
  "trace_keys": {"request_id": "r-9a3b"}
}

Note: The actual audit event store uses a flattened indexable schema; the example above is for implementer clarity.

Retention and residency mapping

| Evidence component | Retention default | Residency constraint | Notes |
|--------------------|-------------------|---------------------|-------|
| Authorization change events | 7 years | Multi-region (primary region of service) | Critical for audits and root-cause of privilege changes |
| CI artifact metadata | 10 years | Same as artifact storage | Immutable checksums required |
| Code review record (PR) | 3 years | Global | Keep text + approvals |
| Deployment rollout logs | 5 years | Region of deployment | Includes canary outcomes and rollback events |
| Forensic snapshots (on IR request) | 2 years after incident closure | Per incident custody | Elevate to legal-hold when required |

SLOs for evidence handoff

- High-severity security incident: evidence bundle assembled and initial delivery to Security/Legal within 2 hours.
- Medium-severity: initial bundle within 8 business hours.
- Audit request (non-emergency): initial response acknowledging scope within 48 hours; final bundle per retention policies.

Operational playbook: assembling an evidence bundle

1) Triage: Security on-call labels the incident and identifies implicated services and time window.
2) Freeze window: trigger short-lived preservation hooks for logs and artifacts (automated via preservation-api).
3) Query provenance store for artifact_id(s) referenced by change_request_id(s). Example KQL:
   - logs | where event_type == "authz_change" and change_request_id == "GH-1428" | project timestamp, principal_id, artifact_id, diff
4) Collect related CI/CD metadata: artifact checksum, build logs, pipeline run id. CLI (internal):
   - auditor-cli fetch-artifact-metadata --artifact artifact://build-20251112-abcdef --output bundle/ci-metadata.json
5) Collect PR and code review snapshot (HTML + approvals). Example:
   - gh api repos/redwood/infra/pulls/1428 --jq '.body,.merged_by,.commits' > bundle/pr-1428.json
6) Pull deployment rollout logs and canary metrics.
7) Pull runtime authorization decision logs for affected windows (see queries).
8) Package manifest (see "Bundle manifest" below).
9) Hash and sign the bundle using the Security keyring; write manifest to immutable evidence-store and create access ticket for IR team.

Bundle manifest (required fields)

- bundle_id: string (e.g., evid-20260228-0001)
- incident_id: existing incident tracker id
- created_by: oncall identity
- time_window_start / end
- services_covered: list of service names
- included_components: list (authz_events, artifact_meta, pr_snapshot, deployments, logs)
- checksums: map of component -> sha256 (recorded as JSON in manifest file)
- signature: base64 signature string

Example manifest (human-readable excerpt):

---manifest---
bundle_id: evid-20260228-0001
incident_id: SEC-2026-102
created_by: ashamenon
services_covered: [admin-portal, redwood-api]
components:
  - authz_events: /bundle/authz-events.ndjson (sha256: e3b0c4...)
  - ci_metadata: /bundle/ci-metadata.json (sha256: 9f8a3d...)
---end---

Query library (examples)

- Find all authorization changes by principal in a time window:
  logs | where event_type == "authz_change" and principal_id == "acct-1024" and timestamp between ("2026-02-01" .. "2026-02-28")

- Map artifact -> deployments:
  artifacts | where artifact_id == "artifact://build-20251112-abcdef" | join deploys on artifact_id | project deploy_time, deployment_id, region, rollout_status

- Extract runtime allow/deny decisions for a request_id:
  logs | where trace_keys.request_id == "r-9a3b" and (event_type == "authz_decision" or event_type == "authz_check") | project timestamp, decision, rule_id, policy_version

Special handling for multi-region and private deployments

- For Private and VPC deployments, evidence collection is constrained by customer residency. The playbook provides an alternate flow where an on-prem agent packages evidence and the manifest is recorded in Redwood's evidence-index with a pointer and custody metadata.
- For cross-border incidents, consult Data Residency & Retention playbook for jurisdictional holds before exporting any logs.

Preservation automation (technical notes)

- preservation-api: internal service that can temporarily increase retention and export a time-bounded slice of logs to evidence-store. Usage: POST /v1/preserve with {service, start, end, requester, reason}.
- provenance-store: append-only datastore for artifact metadata (artifact_id, checksum, pipeline_id, signed_by).
- audit-index: immutable indexed write path for runtime authz events; supports indexed fields principal_id, artifact_id, request_id, service, event_type.

Security controls and privacy considerations

- RBAC for evidence-store: only Security and Legal roles can request signed delivery of a bundle. Eng-sre and Eng-platform receive role-limited tickets to export artifacts.
- Redaction: PII contained within PR text or logs must be redacted before external sharing. Use redaction-api to produce a redaction report included in the bundle.
- Hash-only pointers may be used when cross-border export is not permitted; legal and compliance to approve cross-border retrieval.

Testing and validation

- Quarterly simulation: run an evidence-assembly drill for a synthetic authz change incident to validate SLOs and the signature chain.
- Canary tests: when a change to audit-emission code is merged, run a canary that emits a test authz_change and validate the schema and indexability.

Appendices

A. Example preservation API call (curl)

curl -X POST 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(get-token --service security-oncall)" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://preservation-api.internal/v1/preserve 
  -d '{"service":"admin-portal","start":"2026-02-28T13:00:00Z","end":"2026-02-28T15:00:00Z","requester":"ashamenon","reason":"SEC-2026-102 suspected entitlement change" }'

B. Example auditor-cli commands

# fetch authz events slice
auditor-cli fetch-logs --service admin-portal --start 2026-02-28T13:00:00Z --end 2026-02-28T15:00:00Z --filter 'event_type=authz_change' --out bundle/authz-events.ndjson

# sign bundle
security-cli sign --key evidence-rotate-2026 --file bundle.tar.gz --output bundle.tar.gz.sig

C. Fast checklist for on-call

1) Identify implicated services and scope window.
2) Trigger preservation-api for the window.
3) Record change_request_id(s) and artifact_id(s).
4) Run auditor-cli queries to assemble initial artifacts.
5) Create bundle manifest, sign, and upload to evidence-store.
6) Notify Security/Legal and assign evidence ticket.
